James Fenimore Cooper, The Last of the Mohicans.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/james-fenimore-cooper/the-last-of-the-mohicans

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- James Fenimore Cooper, the author, died 1851 (Wikidata Q167856, P570 = 1851-09-14).

First publication of the text used: 1826 (SE colophon: 'The Last of the Mohicans was published in 1826 by James Fenimore Cooper.'). The Wikipedia infobox gives the first publication as H. C. Carey & I. Lea, released 4 February 1826, country United States.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1826, before 1931, so the US rule settles its origin too. A published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after publication, so this work entered it in 1921.
- Country of origin (United States): the US rule settles the origin, whatever the death year (1851), because the first publication was in the United States before 1931.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
